## Dispatch-time read (PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack`, #6023) — HELD in `pm:queue`, blocked on `hotcrm#1576`

The card's own spine is hotcrm#1576's measured breakage log, and it says to write against that log rather than ahead of it. `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` is outside this seat's repository scope, so this seat cannot read that log or tell when it is complete. Two things unblock the dispatch: (1) a comment here from the hotcrm seat or the maintainer saying the 17.1.0 → 17.3.0 log is complete, with the findings pasted or linked in a form this repo can read; or (2) a ruling that the changeset-only half (the 57+ BREAKING entries with Migration sections) may ship first as the 17.2.0 / 17.3.0 detail sections, with the hotcrm-derived checklist lines added in a second docs-only PR.

When dispatched: docs-only PR touching `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` and nothing else, `skip-changeset`, no rewrite of the 17.0.0 / 17.1.0 sections, every checklist line cited to a changeset hash or a hotcrm finding — the guardrail's dedicated-docs-PR escape hatch, not a rider. Not a governed surface, so it can be armed after review. No nudge will be sent; the seat re-reads this card on each patrol.

## 这张卡的输入变了,而且变强了 —— 连带发现 `upgrading.mdx` 也在缺口里

原卡说本卡的输入是 hotcrm#1576 的「断点表」。维护者纠正了那次演练的方法,连带把本卡的输入也换成了更好的东西:

> 你跑 hotcrm 的时候应该根据升级文档来跑,要模拟这个升级的过程是否顺畅?有没有问题?因为我们最终客户不可能到仓库里来查源码,然后再决定他们的项目怎么升级。

所以 hotcrm#1576 现在是**以客户身份、只用已发布文档**跑一次真实升级 —— 文档站、npm 包里的 CHANGELOG、`os` CLI 的输出、Release 正文,⛔ 不许读本仓源码来决定该怎么做。它的主交付物不再是「断了什么」,而是**「照着文档走,在第几步、因为什么走不下去」**。

那份日志比原来的断点表更适合当本卡的输入:断点表告诉你「代码变了什么」,升级日志告诉你「文档少说了什么」—— 后者才是这张卡要补的东西。

## 范围要扩:`upgrading.mdx` 也在缺口里

原卡只圈了 `releases/v17.mdx`。但客户的**入口**是 `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`,而它同样是断的:

- **`:197`** 的「按大版本的升级清单」表,**v17 只有一行,指向 `/docs/releases/v17#upgrade-checklist`(17.0.0)**。17.1 / 17.2 / 17.3 在这张表里不存在 —— 一个 17.1.0 的客户从这里出发,拿不到任何指向他要跨的那两个版本的线索。
- 该页的整体框架是「同一大版本内移动运行时 = 换 tag、重启,不动元数据」,并有 Callout 明说「Moving the runtime forward one major keeps working with metadata authored against the previous major」。**照这个读法,17.1 → 17.3 就是把镜像 tag 换掉**(`:41` 的示例已经写着 `objectstack:17.3.0`)。
- 而 17.2/17.3 实际带着 `client.projects.*` 的**无别名**重命名、driver 开始强制 `unique`/`indexes[]`、auth audience 默认转 `invite_only`、权限存储读失败改为大声失败 —— 以及 `spec` 的 57 条 BREAKING。

⚠️ 换句话说:**这一页当前的读法,会让客户以为一次带破坏性变更的升级是无操作的。** 这不是「少写了一节」,是一句会误导的话。它是否需要一条「minor 升级也可能带破坏性变更,先看该版本的 checklist」的明确提醒,由本卡一并处理。

### 范围更新

| 文件 | 要做的 |
|:--|:--|
| `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` | 补 **17.2.0** 与 **17.3.0** 的详细段 + 覆盖 17.1→17.3 的 Upgrade checklist |
| `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` | `:197` 的表补齐 v17 各版本条目;复核「换 tag 即可」的框架措辞 |

⛔ 其余不变:**docs-only PR**,不碰代码,不碰 `content/docs/` 的其他页面,不重写已发布的 17.0/17.1 段;⛔ 每条清单项要能追溯到实测或 changeset 自己的 Migration 段,不许凭空编。

**Blocked-by 仍是 hotcrm#1576**,但等的东西换了:等的是那份「文档在哪一步没接住人」的日志。

Addendum to the report above — the two questions the dispatch asked to be answered separately. ⛔ Not a second report; the `os-dev-report` comment above is the canonical one.

## (a) How the BREAKING entries were split, and the counts

**The criterion, stated on the published page itself rather than only here:** an entry is written up when the change **can be reached from something an application ships or operates** — its metadata (a parse / validate / build refusal), its data (a write that used to land, a grant that changes meaning), its own code calling the SDK / REST / CLI, its deployment config, or a plugin it authors. An entry is left to the per-package `CHANGELOG.md` files when the only moving surface is inside the platform's own implementation.

Measured across all 69 package `CHANGELOG.md` files, deduplicated by (short hash + entry text) so a changeset landing in several packages counts once — and note that dedup by hash **alone** is lossy: two hashes here carry two distinct entry texts (`93940d4`, `be21955`), which is why the entry count and the distinct-hash count differ for 17.3.0.

| | 17.2.0 | 17.3.0 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| distinct changelog entries | 204 | 862 |
| entries marking themselves BREAKING | **19** | **100** |
| distinct hashes among those | 19 | 98 |
| **IN — written up in the body** | **19** | **94** |
| **OUT — left to the changelogs** | **0** | **6** |

**17.2.0: nothing was excluded.** All 19 reach an application. The four Console pin refreshes are BREAKING-marked in both releases and are summarized once under their own heading instead of being enumerated as breaking entries — their per-commit content is objectui's changelog, and inlining four pin bodies would be transcription, not triage.

**The six excluded from 17.3.0**, named on the page rather than silently dropped, each with why nothing an app authors or calls reaches it:

| entry | why OUT |
|:--|:--|
| `45b9051` six branded identifier schemas + `EventNameSchema` | TypeScript-only identifier layers, declared and never enforced; no authorable key |
| `50d6c92` `MetadataChangedEventPayloadSchema` | a `metadata:changed` payload nothing ever emitted or consumed |
| `53d3689` `RestApiEndpoint.handlerStatus` + Route Coverage Report shapes | declared, never read; the 501 they described comes from the endpoint executor |
| `7a25e7d` `CLICommandContributionSchema` | an orphan export whose manifest surface is already a tombstone |
| `8619f95` `SendTemplateInput.org` | a declared org-overlay tenant id nothing ever read |
| `4b4d5a3` `FilesystemLoader.list()` | internal loader consistency — reports only the names its own siblings can resolve |

⚠️ **Where the line moved during the work, and why.** My first pass put every ADR-0049 retirement of a *declared-but-inert* key in the OUT bucket, on the reasoning that the corpus was measured at zero producers. That was wrong for this repo: the authorable surface has been strict since 17.0.0 (#4001), so an inert key still sitting in a customer's source **fails their build** — inert upstream is not inert downstream. Those entries moved IN, grouped under one bullet with "delete the key" as the whole migration rather than a subsection each (`7345308`, `15d58db`, `40a93b5`, `4635f3e`, `ee3595c`, `49f0dcf`, `b72db01`, `d173125`, `9e0ba21`). Only surfaces with **no authorable spelling at all** stayed OUT.

Coverage was then verified mechanically rather than asserted: every 7-hex hash in the three new sections was extracted and diffed against the changelog-derived BREAKING set. Result: **19/19** distinct 17.2.0 hashes and **98/98** distinct 17.3.0 hashes appear in the new prose.

## (b) hotcrm#1576 at the time pass 1 finished — waiting, not consumed

**Not delivered. Nothing consumed. Pass 2 is held.**

Read at report time through the public-repo payload channel:

- hotcrm#1576 is **open**, `updatedAt` 2026-09-04T11:20:20Z, carrying exactly two comments — the seat's claim (5539666915) and the maintainer's method correction (5539699172), which re-charters the run as a customer-role, documentation-only upgrade.
- **No upgrade log, no breakage table, no documentation-defect list, and no PR.** Its branch `claude/issue-1576-objectstack-17.3.0` is still at base commit `5e08628f` — nothing has been pushed to it.

So every checklist line I could have written would have had to come from a changeset's own Migration section alone, which is the half the correction comment explicitly said is the weaker input: a changeset tells you *what the code changed*, the upgrade log tells you *what the documentation failed to say* — and the second is what this card exists to fix. Per the dispatch's own instruction for this case, pass 1 shipped and pass 2 is held.

**What pass 2 still owes**, so it can be picked up cold: `### 17.2.0` and `### 17.3.0` under `## Upgrade checklist` on `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`, covering 17.1.0 → 17.3.0 as one path with per-hop notes where a step applies to only one hop; then repoint the two v17.3.0 / v17.2.0 rows in `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` from the `#breaking-changes--migration-in-17X0` anchors to `#1720` / `#1730`, and drop the interim lead paragraph under `## Upgrade checklist`. Every line cited to a hotcrm finding or a changeset Migration section.

## 第二趟的原料到了 —— hotcrm#1576 的升级日志已交付(hotcrm#1577)

PM 记录。这条是**第二趟(17.1.0 → 17.3.0 合并升级清单)的输入**,取代此前 `Blocked-by: hotcrm#1576` 的等待状态。

### ⚠️ 先修正一个前提,是我立卡时写错的

我在 hotcrm#1576 和第一趟 PR 的正文里都写了「hotcrm 钉在 **17.1.0**、这次跨两个 minor」。**错的。** 我按 `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` `main` 的 `package.json` 复核过:12 个 `@objectstack/*` 全是 **`17.2.0`**,从 hotcrm#1442 于 2026-09-01 落地起就是。所以这次演练实测的是**一个 minor**:17.2.0 → 17.3.0。

⛔ **第二趟不要把这份日志当成 17.1.0 → 17.3.0 全程的证据** —— 17.1 → 17.2 那一段**没有人走过**。清单里凡是跨 17.1→17.2 的步骤,要么另找依据,要么明写「未经演练」,⛔ 不许因为「清单要看起来完整」就把它们和实测步骤混在一起写。

### 演练方法与头号读数

按你我商定的方法跑的:**文档是被测对象**,从已发布入口出发,只用客户够得着的东西(文档站、npm tarball 里的 `CHANGELOG.md`、`os` CLI 自己的输出),并且在去找答案**之前**先记下文档在哪一步不够用。

> **文档为这次升级覆盖的步骤数:0。** 十一个破坏点,没有一个能从 `/docs/upgrading` 或 `/docs/releases/v17` 找到。每一个答案都来自 `node_modules/@objectstack/*/CHANGELOG.md`、CLI 打印的诊断,或者对第二台服务器做 A/B 实测。

对「只有文档没有源码,客户能不能完成这次升级」的回答是 **不能**,两处硬停:一处是 `os validate` 拒绝(CLI 诊断写得非常好,坚决的客户能自己过去),另一处是**根本登录不进去**(#15337)。

### 八条文档缺陷 —— 第二趟的工作面

1. **`upgrading.mdx` 根本没有 npm / 依赖升级路径。**「平台运行时」一节只讲 Docker tag 与 systemd 产物置换。最常见的消费形态 —— `package.json` 里的 `@objectstack/*` 钉版本,也就是 `create-objectstack` 脚手架产出的形态 —— **没有任何文档化的升级动作**。需要三步:整组 bump、用你的包管理器重生成 lockfile、移动 `specVersion` / `engines.protocol`。
2. `/docs/releases/v17` 上 **`17.3.0` 这个字符串出现 0 次**,而同一天文档告诉你去钉 `17.3.0`。(第一趟 PR #15333 正在修这条。)
3. `releases/index.mdx` 说「current series: 17.2.0」,`upgrading.mdx:41` 与 `deployment/self-hosting.mdx` 说钉 `17.3.0` —— **文档自己对当前版本的说法互相打架**。已单独立卡 #15332。
4. 每-major 清单表**没有每-minor 行**,而 `upgrading.mdx:192` 恰恰指示读者「你跨过的每一个版本都要读清单」。对 17.1/17.2/17.3 这条指示无法执行。
5. **页面的中心框架「同一个 major 就是移 tag、重启」被这次演练证伪**:两处 authored metadata 被强制修改,`os validate` 与 `os build` 不改就拒绝。
6. **`os migrate meta` 回答「Nothing to migrate」会被读成「你完事了」**,而这个限度没有任何地方写明。它只重放协议链,对 author-time 规则、lint 家族、major 内变化的默认值一个字都不说。那个限度必须写在命令旁边。⚠️ 实测:它回 exit 0「已经 canonical」的那一刻,下面十一条里有**九条**是活的。
7. **每包 `CHANGELOG.md` 才是真正的升级文档**,但文档只在 v10/v11 语境下授权读它。要么把每一个升级者都指过去,要么把它们编译进发布页。

### 十一个破坏点(第二趟清单的正文素材)

### What was wrong

The checklist for 17.3.0 opened with a Callout claiming 17.3.0 shipped an unrecoverable sign-in lockout. **It is false**, and on a customer-facing page it would have told upgraders the platform was broken.

The reading it was built on was misattributed. The server that produced it was started as `objectstack serve --ui` under `NODE_ENV=production`, not `objectstack dev`. The dev-admin seed is by design not armed in that shape — `isDevAdminSeedArmed()` returns false whenever `NODE_ENV` is not `development` — so the account was never created and the `401` was correct behaviour. An ablation holding the tree, the published install and the database path fixed and varying **only the start mode** reproduced the 401 on the serve/production leg and answered 200 on the dev leg, with three further independent shapes all answering 200. The two readings that made it look like a platform defect — a transplanted password hash having no effect, and an authenticating user missing from the database — were artefacts of `rm -rf .objectstack/data` being run against a live server, leaving the process holding deleted file descriptors.
